# ADR 0001: Static site generated by a Python content pipeline

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-10-08

## Context

The previous portfolio was an R Shiny app on shinyapps.io. It had cold starts on the free
tier, required an R runtime to view a mostly static page, and kept resume content in several
hand-edited copies (Rmd, PDF, PNG) that drifted apart. It also lived in a repo that mixed
public portfolio material with private, company-specific application documents.

## Decision

- Store all portfolio content as structured data (`content/*.yaml`, `content/**/*.md`).
- Validate it against strict pydantic models (`extra="forbid"`) before rendering.
- Render static HTML with Jinja and deploy to GitHub Pages from GitHub Actions.
- Keep private application materials out of this repo entirely.

## Consequences

- The site is free, fast, and needs no server.
- One source of truth: the HTML resume and (in a later phase) the PDF resume render from the
  same YAML.
- Content mistakes fail CI instead of shipping.
- Interactive R/Shiny demos, if wanted, live in their own project repos and are linked from
  the Projects page.
